answer: Sybil-resistant economies bind each agent identity to a locked stake verified by a compact on-chain kernel, so voting weight follows capital rather than how many identities a malicious actor can wander between. To control a thousand fake accounts, an attacker must post a thousand bonds; the scarce input becomes money, not CPU. That capital stays frozen like a glacier, carrying real opportunity cost, and any detected double-voting slashes the entire bond. The adversary thus pays in proportion to the influence it seeks and risks losing everything, making mass impersonation unprofitable.
